identity.title: What should a neuron aim for? Designing local objective functions based on information theory

problem.claim: The work addresses how to design local learning goals that make individual artificial neurons self-organize and shape input integration.

gap.claim: The abstract identifies that individual-neuron learning dynamics in globally optimized deep networks are often obscure, motivating a local, interpretable alternative inspired by biological learning.

contributions.claim: It proposes a framework that parameterizes bio-inspired local neuron objectives with Partial Information Decomposition (PID), separating unique, redundant, and synergistic information.
It lets neurons control how feedforward, feedback, and lateral inputs contribute to outputs by selecting their desired unique, redundant, or synergistic roles through a weighted sum of PID terms.
It presents an information-theoretic foundation intended to combine neuron-level interpretability with strong performance under local learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their work advances a principled information-theoretic foundation for local learning strategies by combining PID-parameterized local objectives with neuron-level interpretability.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that their framework enables self-organization between individual artificial neurons through abstract bio-inspired local learning goals.
The authors report that PID-based objectives can be obtained either from intuitive reasoning for a given problem or through numerical optimization.
The authors report that the framework enables strong performance using local learning while providing neuron-level interpretability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Global optimization makes the learning dynamics of individual neurons difficult to understand.
Biological systems are presented as using self-organized local learning with robustness and efficiency despite limited global information.
The work designs local neuron goals using PID, which decomposes source information into unique, redundant, and synergistic components.
A weighted sum of PID terms controls the desired roles of feedforward, feedback, and lateral inputs, with weights derived intuitively or numerically optimized.
The authors position the framework as enabling neuron-level interpretability, strong local-learning performance, and a principled foundation for local learning.

source_observation.claim: The abstract maps each local objective to explicit information roles—unique, redundant, or synergistic—and expresses the choice as a weighted sum of PID terms.

lessons.interpretation: A precise decomposition can connect an interpretable design choice to an optimizable objective.
lessons.application: When proposing a local learning rule, define the information or functional roles of each input stream and write the objective as explicit weighted components.
lessons.exception: This framing may be unsuitable when the task lacks a meaningful outcome variable or when the chosen information decomposition cannot be estimated reliably.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the tasks, datasets, baselines, quantitative performance, or conditions supporting the claim of strong performance.
It does not state which PID definition or numerical optimization procedure is used, nor how the local objectives are implemented or evaluated.
